..
Issued at 125 PM CST Tue Nov 17 2026

A beautiful mid-November day was seen today, with a seasonably 
strong upper level ridge evident by 580+ dam heights overhead and 
WAA return flow pushing temps already in the 50s. GOES satellite 
imagery shows low clouds lifting north and remaining west of the 
CWA, with plentiful sunshine across the region.   

Seasonably Warm & Windy Through Wednesday:

Rest of today will see breezy southerly winds gusting over 30 mph at 
times, especially west of the Mississippi River. Otherwise, 
continued low level WAA will boost temperatures to near 60 degrees 
for some today, allowing to add another above normal day to the 
already top 10 warmest starts to November for Rochester and La 
Crosse. 

A sub 997mb surface low to track into North Dakota resulting in a 
tightening pressure gradient Wednesday and with forecast soundings 
showing 40kts at the top of mixed layer we will see strong southwest 
winds gusting over 35 mph at times during the afternoon. The REFS 
ensemble mean even has some gusts approaching 45 mph near Rochester 
that will be something to watch in later forecasts. Regarding any 
fire weather concerns, GFDI values remain largely in the High 
category, with just a few pixels above 15 in the western CWA. In 
addition, min RH values will be above 40% area-wide likely leading 
to a lower risk of fires spreading out of control. However, if drier 
dewpoints are realized then there may be a higher risk Wednesday. 
Went on the higher end of guidance for highs, with afternoon highs 
topping out near 60 degrees.

Dry mild Thursday with unseasonable high temps in the upper 50s to 
low 60s, as an upper low continues to roll out to the north of LK 
Superior. Breezy southwesterly sfc winds will decrease into the late 
afternoon period. In-between wave upper ridge axis will progress 
across the region for a fair Thu night and sfc wind decrease 
allowing for low temps in the mid 30s north, to the low 40s south.

The local area will be the benefactor of being in the breezy warm 
sector of a rather amplified upper level pattern across the mid 
CONUS on Friday. Another upper wave piece will eject out of western 
CONUS long wave upper trof complex and shear northeastward across 
the northeastern plains. The majority of the ARX CWA could have 
highs in the low to mid 60s, although there will be some mid and 
high level clouds streaming across the area that may act as some 
warming hindrance. Sfc winds and humidity values appear marginal at 
this time for much of higher fire danger threat on Friday, but 
something to keep in mind. The latest ensembles in general agreement 
of LLVL frontogenesis taking place from the upper MS RVR Valley down 
to the southwestern plains Friday night. Initial moisture feed 
limited, but there may be some higher based showers skirting across 
the northwestern CWA after midnight ahead of organizing sfc front 
squeezing eastward acrs central MN and deepening low center pulling 
up into southwestern Ontario.

Saturday and Sunday...This period looks to be a wet showery one 
especially Sat night, as the upstream sfc front pushes in from the 
west. Still some model variance on speed of the FROPA and signs of 
the boundary hanging up with one or two sfc waves rippling along it 
as the southern plains trof base pulls out toward the mid to upper 
MS RVR Valley by Sunday morning. The better rains may occur along and 
post-frontally mid Sat evening into Sunday morning, with several 
medium range model solutions showing the potential for 0.25 to 0.75 
of an inch by Sunday morning across most of the CWA. Despite limited 
instability, strong forcing along the front and some higher level 
thermodynamics may allow for some embedded flashes/thunder Saturday 
evening. Then post-frontal cooling profiles and thicknesses support 
at least a rain-snow mix in the stove pipe region by Sunday morning 
for any lingering precip. Depending on the frontal timing, Sunday 12 
hour highs may be in the mid to upper 40s in the east during the 
morning. Rest of the day to be blustery and a cold advection regime 
with temps in the 30s. Sunday night cold with some wrap around 
clouds and widespread lows in the low to mid 20s.

Early next week looks to continue be cooler and more seasonable with 
passing LLVl and upper ridging making for dry conditions through at 
least Tuesday afternoon.
